title: Eviction certification protocol for KV coherence and memory reclamation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Redwood's multi-GPU serving nodes maintain a distributed KV cache for autoregressive decoding. Under high concurrency and continuous batching, eviction decisions must reclaim GPU memory without dropping prefix state required by in-flight requests. Existing LRU/TTL approaches are insufficient: they either evict needed prefixes (causing correctness regressions) or over-pin entries (causing OOMs). We need a deterministic, auditable protocol that guarantees: (1) no active decode loses required KV state, (2) eviction is safe across GPU shards and batch boundary transitions, and (3) memory reclamation respects TTL and cost signals to optimize throughput/latency trade-offs.

Proposal (Eviction Certification Protocol - ECP):
- Certificate lifecycle: when an entry is considered for eviction, an eviction certificate is issued with metadata: last_access_ts, prefix_tags (set of prefix fingerprints), reference_count_hint, origin_shard_id, and epoch_id.
- Atomic trim marker: eviction certificates create an atomic trim marker per-shard. The runtime uses markers to block compaction of KV slabs for any epoch with active certificates.
- Ghost references: to cover in-flight continuous batches that may reference recently-evicted keys, we keep a lightweight ghost entry (pointer + epoch_id) in CPU memory for up to ghost_ttl ms. Ghosts allow ongoing decode streams to rehydrate the full KV back into GPU memory asynchronously without failing.
- Prefix-aware heuristics: certificates include prefix_tags so the scheduler can avoid evicting entries that share prefixes with currently pinned decode sessions. A per-shard prefix-heat map aggregates recent prefix_tag sightings (sliding window) to bias eviction away from hot prefixes.
- TTL/LRU fusion: eviction score = alpha * normalized_age_score + beta * recency_score + gamma * memory_pressure_score + delta * prefix_conflict_penalty. Coefficients tuned via offline evals.
- Determinism and ordering: shard-level certificate queues are ordered by sequence number derived from last_access_ts and epoch_id; a global coordinator enforces cross-shard conflict resolution for entries that span shards (e.g., KV slices).

Correctness invariants we must guarantee:
1) No-live-decode: if any decode session has an outstanding dependency on a prefix (based on prefix_tags or explicit refcount), the entry cannot be fully reclaimed until the session completes or is preemptively migrated.
2) Rehydration soundness: if a ghost is used to rehydrate an entry, the rehydrated KV must match the authoritative model state for that epoch_id.
3) Memory safety: compaction or slab recycling tied to an eviction certificate must not free memory referenced by any active GPU kernel.
4) Deterministic conflict resolution: given the same input events and epoch sequence, eviction decisions (certificates issued and final reclaimed set) must be reproducible for debugging and audits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/property tests covering: certificate ordering under concurrent access, ghost rehydrate correctness across epochs, and prefix-heatmap biasing effects.
- Integration test in local multi-GPU harness: create 1000 concurrent short/long tokens streams with synthetic prefix overlap; verify zero decode failures and <1% extra latency due to rehydration.
- Chaos test under artificial memory pressure: kill a random worker, assert no corruption and eventual consistency of KV after recovery.
- Benchmarks: end-to-end P95 latency regression <= 5% on high-concurrency workload; memory reclaimed within 2x of theoretical optimal under synthetic TTL distribution.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Ghost entries add CPU memory overhead but allow safe lazy rehydration rather than blocking decodes or duplicating KV on every eviction. We cap ghost_ttl to 200ms by default and make it configurable per-customer tier.
- Prefix tags are a compact fingerprint (64-bit) rather than full prefix hashing to avoid storing long prefix bytes. This may cause rare collisions; the protocol treats collisions conservatively (i.e., assume conflict).
- Global coordinator introduces additional RPCs. To bound latency, coordinator decisions are batched and fall back to shard-local conservative eviction when coordinator is unreachable. This fallback is documented and audited.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged implementation behind runtime.eviction.ecp flag.
2) Internal canary: enable on 2 small internal clusters with synthetic workloads for 1 week.
3) Gradual traffic canary: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4 weeks if metrics pass.
4) Observability: add metrics for certificates_issued, ghosts_created, rehydrations, rehydration_latency, prefix_conflicts, and coordinator_fallbacks.
5) Auto-rollback criteria: rehydration_failure_rate > 0.1% or P95 latency regression > 7% sustained for 30m.

Operational notes:
- Debugging: implement deterministic replay using the certificate event log and epoch replay tool (RIP: runtime/eviction/replay).
- Migration: existing LRU-only config stays default for Dedicated customers until they opt-in.
- Cost: minor CPU overhead for ghost bookkeeping; expected to reduce costly full re-computations under high prefix-sharing workloads.

comments: 2025-01-12 - Marco Ruiz: Initial spike validated ghost rehydration approach with small memory overhead. Raw benchmark shows 18% fewer full recomputes on synthetic prefix-heavy workload.
2025-01-20 - PM review (Riley Chen): Requested explicit rollback criteria and customer opt-in gating for Dedicated clusters. Added to rollout plan.
2025-01-28 - Design review (Lina Gomez): Suggested adding epoch-based deterministic sequence numbers to handle cross-shard slice conflicts. Implemented in latest design iteration.

2025-02-02 - Security review (Priya Menon): No direct data exfil concerns; flagged that prefix_tags are fingerprints and could lead to inference of prefix usage patterns — recommended retention policy and opt-out for high-sensitivity tenants.
2025-02-05 - Infra (Omar Khalid): Noted coordinator fallback must be rate-limited to avoid thundering herd on shard leaders. Added rate-limiter and backoff sketch to the PR.
2025-02-06 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented unit tests and submitted WIP PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8199. Next: integration harness and benchmark run.
